# pengdows.crud (2.0)

> A SQL-first, strongly-typed, testable data access layer for .NET 8. Not an ORM — no LINQ,
> no change tracking — with database-agnostic SQL, safe parameterization, and context-per-tenant
> multi-tenancy across 18 supported database engines.

This file is a curated index, not the full content — it links out to the canonical docs rather
than duplicating them.

Read [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) first for the full API surface, attribute rules (`[Table]`,
`[Column]`, `[Id]` vs `[PrimaryKey]`), `DbMode` connection strategies, and TDD/testing
requirements this repo enforces.

## Multi-tenancy and dynamic provider loading

pengdows.crud uses **context-per-tenant** multi-tenancy (a distinct `DatabaseContext` per
tenant, not row-level `WHERE tenant_id` filtering), with `DbProviderFactory` resolution
config-driven via `DbProviderLoader` for tenants whose provider isn't known at compile time. See
[`docs/multitenancy-dynamic-providers.md`](docs/multitenancy-dynamic-providers.md) for:

- Registering keyed `DbProviderFactory` instances (statically, or dynamically via
  `DbProviderLoader`'s `"DatabaseProviders"` configuration section)
- `AddMultiTenancy` DI registration and the `"MultiTenant"` configuration shape
- Request-time resolution via `ITenantContextRegistry.GetContext(tenant)`
- Protecting a held context from concurrent rotation via `AcquireLease(tenant)`
  (reference-counted, CAS-based; synchronous only — no `AcquireLeaseAsync`/`GetContextAsync`
  in this version, since 2.0's `IDatabaseContextFactory` has no async `CreateAsync`)
- Lifecycle: `Invalidate`/`InvalidateAll`, `ContextCreated`/`ContextRemoved` events,
  `maxTenantCount` cardinality cap (admission is atomic — safe under concurrent distinct-tenant
  creation), case-insensitive tenant-ID lookup

## Other documentation

- [`RELEASE_NOTES_1.0_TO_2.0.md`](../RELEASE_NOTES_1.0_TO_2.0.md) — breaking changes from 1.0
- [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) — overall architecture, including a simpler
  DI-only (non-registry) multi-tenancy pattern
- [`docs/connection-management-guide.md`](docs/connection-management-guide.md) — `DbMode`
  connection strategies
- [`docs/parameter-naming-convention.md`](docs/parameter-naming-convention.md) — per-operation
  SQL parameter naming (`i{n}`, `s{n}`, `w{n}`, `k{n}`, `v{n}`, `j{n}`, `b{n}`)
- [`docs/supported-databases.md`](docs/supported-databases.md) — the 18 supported database
  engines and dialect capability notes. Percona Server for MySQL, Citus, TimescaleDB, and
  Fujitsu Enterprise Postgres are not distinct `SupportedDatabase` values — all four are
  detected at runtime and delegate to the MySQL/PostgreSQL dialect (verified live against
  real containers; see the "Verified PostgreSQL/MySQL-compatible forks" note in that file).
  SingleStore *is* a distinct `SupportedDatabase` value (unlike those four) because it reports
  a generic, indistinguishable MySQL version string and needs its own runtime probe
  (`SELECT @@memsql_version`) to detect at all. FlatFile
  ([pengdows.flatfile](https://github.com/pengdows/pengdows.flatfile)) is also a distinct value
  with its own partial dialect. Sybase and Db2 (IBM Db2 LUW) each have their own dedicated
  `SybaseDialect`/`Db2Dialect` (not delegating forks) — see the "SingleStore", "FlatFile",
  "Sybase", and "IBM Db2 (LUW)" notes in that file.
- [`docs/transactions.md`](docs/transactions.md) — transaction/savepoint usage; do not use
  `TransactionScope` (incompatible by design — see `CLAUDE.md`)

## Related

- **`pengdows.crud-2.0`** is one version of this library in a multi-version repository; a newer
  version lives alongside it (`pengdows.crud-2.1`/`pengdows.crud`), with a further-expanded
  tenant-context API (`GetContextAsync`, `AcquireLeaseAsync`, built on async `DatabaseContext`
  creation) not present in 2.0 — do not assume API parity across versions without checking
  source directly.
